- Confirm publisher account prerequisites (MPN/AAD tenant linkage).
- Which offer types do you recommend for a SaaS connector (App registration + ARM manifest vs. SaaS connector)?
- What artifacts do you need for technical verification and security review (manifest, ARM templates, test subscription, SOC2 evidence)?
- Expected timeline to pass your technical gate and get co-sell nomination?

I've attached a quick spreadsheet with our current artifacts and a single point of contact.

Attachments: Contoso_Marketplace_Questions.xlsx (worksheet: artifact_inventory)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contoso: Azure Marketplace listing & co-sell intake — kickoff

Alex — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. Happy to run point from Redwood's side. Below is a runnable onboarding playbook (technical + co-sell) and a short mutual-action plan. I'll send a calendar invite after we confirm availability.

Redwood technical onboarding checklist (high level) — please provide or confirm:
1) Publisher account & tenant mapping: MPN ID, Publisher email, tenant ID.
2) Offer model: SaaS connector recommended for FraudShield; we need the SaaS REST endpoints and an AAD app registration pattern. (If you prefer an ARM-based VM offer, call it out.)
3) Offer manifest draft: package.json/manifest + plan SKUs.
4) Deployment artifact: ARM template (if applicable) or sample SaaS provisioning flow.
5) Test tenant: test subscription + test user accounts (we use these for automated smoke tests).
6) Security/compliance evidence: SOC2 report (redacted OK), data flow diagram, retention policy, and access control docs.
7) Connectivity: any IP allowlists, callback URLs, and webhook signing keys.
8) Support & billing contacts for co-sell registration.

Redwood actions:
- Technical validation (SoJ): validate manifest, run smoke tests, signoff on publisher metadata. Owner: Soojin Lee.
- Co-sell enablement (commercial): register opportunity with MSFT co-sell team, nomination docs. Owner: Marissa Cole.
- Runtime & perf guidance: short doc on model/instance sizing and expected latency/cost tradeoffs. Owner: Jonas Weber.

Proposed mutual-action plan (tentative):
- Day 0 (this week): confirm tenant + test account + manifest draft.
- Day 3-5: Redwood runs manifest validation and initial smoke tests.
- Day 7-10: Security evidence review + co-sell registration packet assembled.
- Day 14: Target for first co-sell nomination submission to MSFT.

Attachments: Redwood_Azure_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf (checklist + required artifact templates)

Can you share tenant ID and a draft manifest? Also indicate if you have a preferred timeline that differs from the plan above.

Thanks — I'll coordinate the invite.

Aditya Rao
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Got it — I'll take the technical validation. Quick readout of next steps and what I need from Contoso during the sync: 

1) Confirm test credentials and tenant invitation for test@contoso-cloud.com (we need contributor access on the test subscription).
2) Provide AAD app id + redirect URIs used for provisioning flows.
3) Share webhook signing key or verification method for event webhooks used in provisioning.
4) Confirm whether the offer will support single-tenant or multi-tenant provisioning (affects app registration and manifest fields).

I'll run the Redwood smoke tests (manifest lint, provisioning smoke, auth flow, and basic API health checks) and produce a short validation report. If all goes well we can hit the Day 7 nomination target. I've attached a short test plan template.
